description:
Reserve the paths snapshot export stages from the captured image, so a document or asset reference to a tracker path reuses the captured bytes instead of overwriting them.

## Background

- Export assembly stages captured tracker state first (`copy_jit_state`, `crates/jit/src/commands/snapshot.rs` ~142, called ~537), then documents and assets (`create_document_snapshot` ~542). `capture_file` (~259-282) writes each document or asset destination unconditionally. When a document references `.jit/config.toml` with scanning skipped and export runs `--at` an older commit, the export replaces the captured declaration with historical bytes. Issue records and asset references collide the same way.
- Story `19404174` sol checkpoint review, finding 2 (REQ-04, "stored bytes … read from one captured image"). Invoker ruling: routine. Paths staged by `copy_jit_state` are reserved, and one test owns the property.
- Epic criterion: `b697a3f7` REQ-19.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Every path `copy_jit_state` stages is reserved: a document or asset reference to a reserved path reuses the captured bytes and their manifest entry and never overwrites the staged file.
- [hard] REQ-02: One test owns the property: exporting `--at` an older commit with a document that links `.jit/config.toml` keeps the captured declaration bytes in the export. Issue-record and asset collisions are covered by the same rule, with no per-kind tests.
- [hard] REQ-03: Exports without such a collision are byte-identical to today's.
title: Snapshot export reserves the paths it stages from the captured image
